Electrochemical characterizations of LPSC and LPSC-MF electrolytes. a) Nyquist plots of Li6+3xP1� xMgxS5Cl1� 2xF2x electrolytes (x=0, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3) at 25°C. b) Arrhenius plots of the temperature-dependent ionic conductivities of Li6+3xP1� xMgxS5Cl1� 2xF2x electrolytes with different doping contents. c) Ionic conductivities and activation energy of Li6+3xP1� xMgxS5Cl1� 2xF2x against different doping contents. d) Stable current response of LPSC and LPSC-MF (x=0.1) at different voltages. Li6+3xP1� xMgxS5Cl1� 2xF2x (x=0.1) electrolyte as the optimal doping amount and denote the electrolyte as LPSC-MF. figures.caption: Figure 4. Analysis of interfacial reaction and products. a) Cyclic voltammetry profile of Li/LPSC/LPSC+C and Li/LPSC-MF/LPSC-MF+C semi- blocking cell at 0.1 mVs� 1. Ex situ Raman spectra results of b) LPSC and c) LPSC-MF in different voltage states of the LiCoO2/sulfide-SE/Li cells. Interfacial compositional alteration by XPS analysis after cycling over d) S 2p and e) P 2p spectra at Li/LPSC and Li/LPSC-MF interface. XPS depth profiling analysis of the Li anode/electrolyte interface. Overall spectra evolution of f) F 1s with different etch level at the Li/LPSC-MF interface. SEM images of lithium metal surface of Li symmetric cells assembled with h) LPSC and i) LPSC-MF after short circuit. Schematic illustrations of interface reaction and Li dendrite growth at the g) Li/LPSC interface and Li/LPSC-MF interface.
